title: The negative Koszul tail augmentation has the full Koszul complex as its cone
statement: Let A be a commutative ring, r a natural number, f:Fin(r)->A and e a natural number. Use the tail I with terms wedge^(n+1) A^r and negative Koszul differential on the powers f_i^(e+1), its augmentation I->A[0], and the inclusion A[0]->K from [def-sc-koszul-open-system]. Extend all chain complexes by zero to integer cochain degree -n. Let u be the extended augmentation. Then there exists an isomorphism of cochain complexes Cone(u) -> K(f_i^(e+1)) [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex] whose composite with the right cone inclusion equals the extended inclusion A[0]->K. No derived-category localization or quasi-coherent object is required.

source.place: Section 36.9 (Tag 08CX), opening construction of I and its Koszul triangle; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08CX because the local TeX source is absent.

proof.text: Let u be the extended tail augmentation from [def-sc-koszul-open-system]. At cochain degree n the cone has terms I^(n+1) plus A[0]^n. If n<0 its second summand is zero and its first is K^n; if n=0 its first summand is zero and its second is A, identified with K^0 by the inverse of exteriorPower.zeroEquiv. If n>0 both summands vanish. Use the appropriate biproduct projection for the forward map and inclusion for the inverse, obtaining degreewise inverse maps to the full Koszul complex [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex].

The mapping-cone differential on the tail summand is the negative of the tail differential, cancelling the negative sign in I. The only off-diagonal nonzero term is from degree -1 to degree zero: it is u, whose degree-zero component is koszulBoundary followed by exteriorPower.zeroEquiv. The degree-zero identification cancels that equivalence, giving the full Koszul differential. This verifies every chain-map square, so the degreewise inverses give an isomorphism of cochain complexes.

The right cone inclusion is zero in every degree other than zero. At degree zero the constructed isomorphism sends A to K^0 by the inverse of exteriorPower.zeroEquiv, exactly koszulOpenKoszulInclusion. Equality of all components gives the required morphism equality. When r=0 the tail is zero and the cone is A[0]; for the zero ring all terms are zero.

lean.statement: theorem koszulOpen_module_cone_comparison (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (r : ℕ) (f : Fin r → A) (e : ℕ) : let u := HomologicalComplex.extendMap (koszulOpenAugmentation A r f e) ComplexShape.embeddingDownNat ∃ c : CochainComplex.mappingCone u ≅ (ExteriorAlgebra.koszulComplex A r (fun i ↦ f i ^ (e + 1))).extend ComplexShape.embeddingDownNat, CochainComplex.mappingCone.inr u ≫ c.hom = HomologicalComplex.extendMap (koszulOpenKoszulInclusion A r f e) ComplexShape.embeddingDownNat
